Commentary.Commentary: A pitiable toil for the Lankans. They struggled for the whole of Day 2 and even though started Monday nicely, were never able to keep the pressure on consistently. Lahiru Kumara bowled his heart out, with a 4-fer while the others just went through the motions. We now have 14 overs left in the day. How many wickets can the Kiwis prize out? Can the Lankan openers see off this tricky period?

Now, about Tom Latham. His first Test century in more than a year. And boy, has he made it memorable. There might not have been any pressure but he did not play loose cricket. Attached a price tag to his wicket and tired the Lankans out. He alone faced 489 balls - which is more than 81 overs! LATHAM BECOMES THE SECOND KIWI OVERALL TO CARRY HIS BAT THROUGH AND THE FIRST TO DO SO IN NEW ZEALAND!

Nearly everyone contributed in this mammoth total. Williamson-Latham's 162-run stand is the best but there were as many as 4 50-plus partnerships. 8 out of the 10 stands crossed 20 and at least faced 15 balls each. Which means that pressure was not only from one end but from both ends.
A fabulous batting display by New Zealand. Leave aside Tom Latham. He was in his own world. But what about the rest? This is how a batting scorecard should look like.

OUT! Sri Lanka have picked up their 7th wicket in the form of a run out! Great piece of fielding and who better than the captain to lead from the front? Full and outside off, Southee punched it towards cover and set off for a quick single. It was not a bad call at all to be honest. He saw that Chandimal was at wide mid off and had to cover some distance, pick up the ball and then aim at the stumps at the bowler's end with only one stick to aim. How many times out of 10 does that happen these days? Probably 1. Unfortunately for Southee, this was that 1 time. Chandimal charged in from wide mid off, swooped onto the ball and then released it quickly. The key was that he went on the bounce and did not attempt a full throw. Hit the stumps and it was referred upstairs. Replays show that Southee was more than a yard short.
Direct hit! Is Southee gone?

How will the Lankan bowlers be feeling? Russel Arnold tries to get into their mindset by having a chat with their bowling coach Rumesh Ratnayake. Ratnayake says that the Lankans should have got at least 5 wickets yesterday but the execution was not correct. Hopes to rectify those mistakes today. Adds further that the team sometimes bowled in the wrong areas and the Kiwis pounced. Also feels that the strong wind was a cause of obstruction for the Lankans. And feels for the fact that the fast bowlers are playing after a long time for the visitors. But having said all of this, does not want to make it as an excuse.

PITCH REPORT - Scott Styris is alongside Mark Richardson doing the pitch report. The latter says that it still looks a very good track for batting. The colour has grown brown and the life seems to have gone out of the pitch. Little bit of grass is around, he says but for how long will it be able to hold the surface together, he is not sure. Does not see too many cracks around but does observe some starting to develop.

Tom Latham is having a chat with Mark Richardson. The current opener says that it feels pleasant to have got past the century line. Adds that being involved in partnerships was the key to bat deep. Feels that he has been hitting the ball pretty well and he just believed in himself, working on little areas here and there. On the runs not coming in the previous knocks in spite of him being in good touch, Latham admits that he was getting frustrated but he just kept believing that trusting doing the regular things would eventually fetch him runs. On his love affair with this ground, Tom says that the pitch over here is very good for batting and he enjoys playing over here. On the adjustment to the conditions from those in the UAE, Latham says that the first 20-30 minutes are the key and one can then play his shots.
WEATHER - Slightly cloudy conditions today with plenty of breeze around. That should help the bowlers a bit. We haven't seen much cloud in the last two days.

Bad bowling or a flat pitch? Perhaps both. There is nothing in the track and the Lankans have not been able to even string successive maiden overs to apply  any sort of pressure. 37 overs are left in the day and the Kiwis look well-poised to take the lead by Stumps itself. Join us back at 4 pm local time (0300 GMT).

If there was any momentum for the Lankans, IF AT ALL ANY, Williamson snapped it in the first three balls that he faced. Three boundaries and Sri Lanka were on the back foot straightaway. He has since then scored at will, going at a strike rate of over 100 and it has not got down even once. Latham, at the other end, has looked calm and composed as ever, just blocking and keeping the balls out.

The session started with the Kiwis 1 down and has ended in the same manner. A wicket-less session for the Lankans. They induced a couple of edges but none went to hand. Probably, that got them frustrated, as they were simply not able to breach the defenses of Latham or Williamson. Result? 116 runs have been scored in 25 overs. Ouch. That is almost at 5 runs an over.

If at least the line can be consistent, the batsmen can still commit mistakes and wickets might come. Join us back at 1.40 pm local time (0040 GMT).

The hosts started well with the bat and were very cautious in their approach. Both openers played some delightful shots and got a 50 run-stand as well. They were looking poised to go unharmed into the break when Raval lost his concentration.

Something to smile for Sri Lanka heading into the break. It was an excellent session for New Zealand, barring that last-ball blemish. They came in the morning and wrapped up the Sri Lankan innings very quickly with Southee bagging a 6-fer.

LUNCH ON DAY 2, NEW ZEALAND TRAIL BY 223!
